en.title: Grocery shopping
en.goal: Make a shopping list and say what you eat or don't eat in everyday life.

phrases.scenario: Someone asks if you like meat, and you like it a lot. What do you answer?
Someone asks about your eating habits and you eat vegetables every day. What do you say?
You're a vegetarian and need to tell the waiter you don't eat meat. What do you say?
At the supermarket, someone asks what you're going to get. What do you answer?

phrases.t: Vegetables are good for your health.
Rice and pasta are my favorite dishes.
The sugar and the salt are on the table.

negation-partitif.title: "Je ne mange pas DE viande" — where did the "la" go?
negation-partitif.body: After a negation with ne... pas, the articles du/de la/des disappear and become just de (or d' before a vowel): je mange de la viande → je ne mange pas de viande. This rule applies to almost every negation of quantity in French — it's worth paying attention to it.

le-marche-tradicao.title: Beyond the supermarket: the marché
le-marche-tradicao.body: In many French cities and villages, besides the supermarket, it's a tradition to shop at the marché — an open-air market that usually takes place once or twice a week, with stalls of local producers selling fresh fruit, vegetables, cheese, meat and bread. It's also a social moment: many people run into neighbors and acquaintances there.
